check_service_status.description: Check whether JokeAPI is answering, how quickly, and how much of this minute's request budget is left. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being throttled, being down for maintenance and being refused by the service's CDN are told apart, because they call for different responses: the first clears within a minute, the second is tracked on the service's status page, and the third usually clears on its own.

mock_response.message: JokeAPI is up and answering, with 119 of 120 requests left this minute.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

get_api_info.description: Report what the service currently holds: its version, how many jokes there are, which categories, flags, types and formats exist, which joke ids are valid in each language and how many of those jokes are safe. This is the action to run before filtering, and the one that says whether an id range you want to use exists at all.
get_api_info.name: get_api_info

get_joke.description: Get one joke, filtered however you need: by category, by language, one-line or two-part, with flagged jokes excluded and safe mode on. The joke comes back with its whole text in one field ready to post, as well as its setup and delivery separately, so a one-line joke and a two-part joke can be handled the same way.

joke.setup: Why do programmers always mix up Halloween and Christmas?
joke.text:
Why do programmers always mix up Halloween and Christmas?
Because Oct 31 == Dec 25.

get_joke.name: get_joke

parameters.description: Which kinds of joke to draw from. Pick several to draw from any of them, or none to draw from all of them. The service's own aliases are accepted too, so a category read off an earlier joke works as a filter here: Miscellaneous means Misc, Coding and Development mean Programming, and Halloween means Spooky.
parameters.name: categories

parameters.description: Do not serve jokes carrying any of these flags. This is the filter that keeps a public-facing workflow safe: the catalogue includes a Dark category and jokes many people would not want posted under their name. Excluding nsfw, racist, sexist and explicit is a sensible floor; turn on Safe mode as well if nothing explicit can get through.
parameters.name: blacklist_flags

parameters.description: Only draw one-line jokes, or only setup-and-delivery ones. Leave it empty for either. Every joke comes back with its whole text in one field regardless, so this is for when the shape matters - a two-part joke can be posted with its delivery held back.
parameters.name: joke_type

parameters.description: The language to draw jokes in, as a two-letter code or a language name. Jokes exist in English, German, Czech, Spanish, French and Portuguese; run Get languages for the current list and how many jokes each holds. Beware that the service also lists Italian and Russian, which it translates its error messages into but has no jokes in - asking for those is reported here rather than coming back empty. Leave it empty for English.
parameters.name: language

parameters.description: Serve only jokes the service considers safe for everyone. This is broader than the flags: it also excludes the whole Dark category and jokes whose language or references make them explicit even unflagged. Turn it on for anything customer-facing.
parameters.name: safe_mode

parameters.description: Only draw from this range of joke ids, written as 0-99. Ids are positions in a language's own joke file, so a range means different jokes in each language; Get API info reports which ids exist in which. Leave it empty to draw from all of them.
parameters.name: id_range

get_joke_by_id.description: Get one specific joke by its id, for re-reading a joke an earlier step found or for pinning a workflow to a joke you have chosen. Ids are positions in a language's own joke file, so the same id is a different joke in each language and the language travels with it.

joke.joke: I invented a new word: Plagiarism!
joke.text: I invented a new word: Plagiarism!

get_joke_by_id.name: get_joke_by_id

parameters.description: The joke's numeric id. Ids start at 0. A full JokeAPI request URL carrying an idRange is accepted too, which is what you get from the service's own Try It form.
parameters.name: joke_id

parameters.description: The language to draw jokes in, as a two-letter code or a language name. Jokes exist in English, German, Czech, Spanish, French and Portuguese; run Get languages for the current list and how many jokes each holds. Beware that the service also lists Italian and Russian, which it translates its error messages into but has no jokes in - asking for those is reported here rather than coming back empty. Leave it empty for English.
parameters.name: language

get_joke_of_the_day.description: Pick one joke for a day and keep picking that same joke all day. The service draws at random on every call, so a daily post that retries, or that two people run an hour apart, tells two different jokes for the one day. This one is fixed by the date: the same date always gives the same joke, and tomorrow gives a different one. It honours the same filters as a normal draw, so a safe joke of the day stays safe. Add a seed of your own to have two workspaces tell different jokes on the same day.

get_jokes.description: Get up to ten jokes in one request, with the same filters as a single draw. No joke is returned twice in one batch. The service changes the shape of its answer when you ask for more than one joke; this always returns a list, so a step that reads it does not break when someone raises the count from one to two. Fewer jokes than asked for means that is all that matched, which is reported rather than treated as a failure.

get_language_code.description: Turn a language name into the two-letter code the other actions take. The service searches its language list loosely, so German, Deutsch and a near miss all resolve. The answer also says whether that language has any jokes, because a code on its own does not: it resolves Italian quite happily, and there are no Italian jokes.
get_language_code.display_str_template: Get the JokeAPI language code for {0}.
get_language_code.name: get_language_code

parameters.description: The language to look up, by name. Spelling it the way it is spelt in that language works too.
parameters.name: language

list_categories.description: List the joke categories the service currently serves, and the aliases that resolve onto them. Worth having because a joke's own record says its category is Misc while a person filtering will as happily type Miscellaneous, and every category field in this integration takes either.
list_categories.name: list_categories

list_flags.description: List the flags a joke can carry, which are the flags a filter can exclude. Run it before building a filter so a workflow excludes everything it means to, rather than the four someone remembered.
list_flags.name: list_flags

list_languages.description: List the languages jokes exist in, with how many jokes each holds and how many of those are safe, alongside the languages the service translates its error messages into. These are two different sets, which is the point of this action: Italian and Russian are real JokeAPI languages with no jokes in them at all, so a workflow that picks a language off the wrong list gets nothing and cannot tell why.
list_languages.name: list_languages

search_jokes.description: Find jokes containing a word or phrase, anywhere in the joke and whatever its case. Use it to pull a joke that fits an occasion, or to check whether the catalogue has anything about a subject at all. Nothing matching is an empty result here rather than a failed step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. The service returns up to ten matches drawn at random from however many there were, and never reports how many that was, so treat the result as a sample rather than the first page of a ranked list.

description: Pull jokes into a workflow from JokeAPI, an open catalogue of around 1,370 jokes in six languages with unusually fine filters. Draw one joke or up to ten, narrow by category, language and one-line or two-part, search for a joke about a subject, look one up by id, or pick a joke of the day that stays the same all day so a scheduled post never tells two. Every joke arrives with its whole text in one field whichever type it is, and with the content flags it carries, so a public-facing workflow can exclude anything it would not want to post: blacklist the flags you object to, or turn on safe mode and let the service decide. No account or API key is required.
